cards.explanation: The answer is the longer one. Daniel says, “…and the longer one grew up later.” So the tall horn showed up after the short one and still ended up taller. Late to the shift and finished with the biggest batch, friends.
The answer is False. Daniel says no animal could stand against the ram. There was also no deliverance from his power. He did as he pleased, and that's the whole picture.
The word is great. Daniel says the ram “…did as he pleased and became great.” Three directions, nobody standing against him, and the verse lands on great. I'd have settled for a clean countertop.
The answer is horn. Daniel sees a goat “…with a prominent horn between his eyes…” One big horn right in the middle, which makes this goat easy to pick out of a crowd.

The goat rushes at him with furious power. That's how Daniel puts it: the goat “…rushed at him with furious power.” Verse 7 adds that he approached the ram in a rage. No warm-up lap, no polite hello. Just full speed from the start.

The goat throws him down and tramples him. That's what Daniel sees: the goat “…threw him to the ground and trampled him…” The ram was powerless to stand against him. The same ram that did as he pleased is now thrown down and trampled.

The answer is True. Daniel says that when the large horn broke off, four prominent horns came up in its place. They pointed toward the four winds of heaven. One horn goes out and four come in. That's quite the replacement policy.

The answer is False. This horn starts little and doesn't stay that way. Daniel says it grew extensively toward the south, the east and the Beautiful Land. Then verse 10 says it grew as high as the host of heaven. Little is just where it starts.

The answer is True. Daniel says the horn “…cast down some of the host and some of the stars to the earth and trampled them.” Notice it says some, not all. It's a heavy moment, so I'll just say it plainly.

The horn prospers in whatever it does. Daniel says it “…flung truth to the ground and prospered in whatever it did.” The host and the daily sacrifice were given over to it. This is a heavy part of the vision, and Daniel doesn't soften it.

The holy one asks how long until it is fulfilled. He says, “How long until the fulfillment of the vision…” It's about the daily sacrifice, the rebellion and the trampled sanctuary. Everybody asks how long when they've been standing in a slow line at the bank.
The answer is True. The reply is, “It will take 2,300 evenings and mornings; then the sanctuary will be properly restored.” The trampling has an end. After the count, the sanctuary is restored.

The answer is Gabriel. The voice by the Ulai calls Gabriel by name and tells him to explain the vision to Daniel. Gabriel is an angel who stands in the presence of God (Luke 1:19). Daniel had been trying to understand the vision, and now help is on the way, friends.

The vision concerns the time of the end. Gabriel tells Daniel, “understand that the vision concerns the time of the end.” So this isn't a small vision about one afternoon. Gabriel points it toward the end.
The answer is False. Daniel says Gabriel “…touched me, helped me to my feet…” So Daniel doesn't stay face down. Gabriel picks him up and then keeps talking.
The word is king. Gabriel says, “…the large horn between his eyes is the first king.” So the big horn stands for a person, and the goat stands for the king of Greece.

The answer is True. Gabriel says these are four kingdoms that will rise from that nation, “…but will not have the same power.” So four kingdoms replace the broken horn, and Gabriel says they will not have the same power.
The answer is False. Gabriel says, “His power will be great, but it will not be his own.” Great power, but not his own. I won't guess whose it is, because the verse doesn't say.
The word is deceit. Gabriel says, “Through his craft and by his hand, he will cause deceit to prosper…” This king is skilled in intrigue, and his deceit does well. It's a heavy thing to hear.

He will be broken off but not by human hands. Gabriel says, “Yet he will be broken off, but not by human hands.” He stands against the Prince of princes, and he's still broken off. The verse says no more than that, so I won't add anything.

It's because the vision concerns the distant future. Gabriel says, “Now you must seal up the vision, for it concerns the distant future.” Gabriel says the vision is true, then tells Daniel to seal it. The reason is in the same verse.
Daniel goes about the king's business. He says, “Then I got up and went about the king’s business.” Sick days end and the work doesn't. He goes back to it after the vision and the days he lay ill.

The answer is False. Daniel says, “I was confounded by the vision; it was beyond understanding.” So he doesn't walk away with all of it figured out. He saw it and Gabriel explained it, and he still says that.
